title: Validate metering invariants for proxy-transformed streaming fragments
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Intermediary proxies and edge gateways sometimes transform streaming fragments (whitespace normalization, gzip recompression, JSON pretty-printing, re-chunking, base64 wrapping for attachments). These transformations can shift tokenizer boundaries or change raw byte counts so the server-side metering pipeline attributes a different token count than what the customer/client observed, causing billing discrepancies and confusing support tickets. This ticket scopes design and implementation work to ensure metering invariants hold (or are auditable) when fragments are transformed in-flight.
tasks: Define canonical fragment representation and transformation-safe hashing protocol (canonicalize whitespace, predictable newline handling, and encoding normalization)
Add optional fragment metadata on the wire: client_raw_hash, client_declared_bytes, transform_version headers for WS/HTTP streaming frames
Instrument metering pipeline to persist three values per fragment: raw_wire_hash, canonical_hash, canonical_token_count
Implement deterministic canonicalization library used in both client-side test harness and server-side pipeline
Create synthetic proxy harness that applies typical transformations (gzip recompress, indenting JSON, chunk-rechunk) for staging tests
Run end-to-end staging run: compare client_token_count, canonical_token_count, and server_billed_tokens; record deltas
Implement reconciliation job to retroactively tag mismatched fragments and emit corrective ledger adjustments when policy allows
Add alerts and dashboard panels: fragment-mismatch-rate, median-delta-tokens, top origins (proxy/IP/region) by mismatch
Document the invariant: canonical_token_count is authoritative for billing; client_raw_hash provides provenance for dispute resolution
Add migration plan for historical data (backfill canonical_hash where raw bytes are retained)
acceptance_criteria: Canonicalization library exists and is language portable; unit tests cover edge cases (Unicode normalization, CRLF vs LF, BOM stripping)
Metering pipeline stores raw_wire_hash and canonical_hash for every streaming fragment in staging and production (opt-in for legacy tenants)
Staging harness produces >1000 simulated transformed sessions and measured token-delta distribution is recorded
Reconciliation job correctly identifies and tags mismatches and generates ledger-correction proposals (no automatic charge reversals without review)
Dashboards show mismatch rate <= 0.02% for first 72-hour pilot; any mismatch above threshold creates an automatic incident ticket
Customer support playbook documented with steps to retrieve fragment provenance, validate canonical hash, and escalate billing disputes
notes: This is an investigation-first ticket: goal is to make transformations auditable and to reduce manual billing disputes
We must avoid adding per-fragment CPU cost that violates latency SLOs; canonicalization should be cheap and incremental

Policy decision required: whether to bill based on client-observed tokens, canonical tokens, or choose a reconciliation policy. Default proposal: canonical tokens for billing but retain provenance to honor disputes
Edge-case: proxies that intentionally truncate or merge fragments. Detection heuristics will flag these but may require legal/ops action for customer remediation
Privacy: raw_wire_hash is a non-reversible fingerprint; avoid storing raw fragment content unless retention policy and customer consent allow it
